en.value: Dejection: ‘An Ode’ is written by:

english.explanation: Dejection: An Ode is written by Samuel Taylor Coleridge in 1802 and was published the same year in The Morning Post, a London daily newspaper. The poem in its original form was written to Sara Hutchinson, a woman who was not his wife, and discusses his feelings of love for her. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: ‘Table Talk’ is a collection of essays by:

english.explanation: Table Talk is a collection of essays by the English cultural critic and social commentator William Hazlitt. It was originally published as two volumes, the first of which appeared in April, 1821. Hazlitt was a English essayist, dramatist and literary critic. He is now considered one of the greatest critics and essayists in the history of the English language. He was also a finest art critic of his age. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Walter Scott is a______novelist.

english.explanation: Walter Scott was a Scottish historical novelist, poet and playwright. Many of his works remain classics of European and Scottish literature. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: The phrase ‘‘negative capability’’ is associated with:

english.explanation: The phrase negative capability is associated with John Keats. It was coined in one of the letters to his brother. Keats regarded Shakespeare as the prime example of negative capability, attributing to him the ability to identify completely with his characters, and to write about them with empathy and understanding. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Charles Darwin's Origin of Species was published in the year:

english.explanation: On the Origin of Species is a work of scientific literature by Charles Darwin that is considered to be the foundation of evolutionary biology. It was published on 24th November, 1859. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Weena is a character in H.G. Well's novel:

english.explanation: Weena is a fictional character in the novel The Time Machine, written by H.G. Wells in 1895 on the concept of time travels to 802, 701 A.D. using his time machine, to find that human have evolved into two species: the Eloi, the leisure class and the Morlocks, the working class. Weena was an Eloi girl. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: ‘Shooting an Elephant’ is an essay by:

english.explanation: Shooting an Elephant is an essay by British writer George Orwell, first published in the literary magazine new writing in late 1936. George Orwell was his pen name although his name was Eric Arthur Blair. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Moll White and Will Wimble are:

english.explanation: Moll White and Will Wimble are the characters created by Joseph Addison. Moll White is a character in the essay On Witchcraft, story of Moll White, a old woman who was regarded as a witch in the locality. Will Wimble is another character by Addison who is about forty and fifty. He has no specific business to do. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘To enliven morality with wit and temper wit with morality’’ is the professed aim of:

english.explanation: The Spectator was a daily publication founded by Joseph Addison and Richard Steele in England, lasting from 1711 to 1712. Each Paper, or number, was approximately 2500 words long and the original run consisted of 555 numbers. In Number 10, Mr. Spectator states that The Spectator will aim ‘‘to enliven morality with wit, and to temper wit with morality.’’ Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Hazlitt called_____depiction world as ‘‘artificial reality’’.

english.explanation: Hazlitt called Richardson's depiction world as artificial reality. In Clarissa, Richardson relates the events of eleven months in a cool million words, unfolding them in something like real time but Hazlitt called it artificial reality. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: The Royal Society of London was established in:

english.explanation: The Royal Society of London was established in 1660 to bring together leading scientific minds of the day, and became an international network for practical and philosophical investigation of the physical world. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Cavalier Poets supported _____in the civil war.

english.explanation: The cavalier poets were a group of seventeenth-century English poets that supported Charles I during the English Civil War (1642-1651). They directly opposed the parliamentarians who were attempting to overthrow the king. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Conceit and Wit’’ are the features of:

english.explanation: Conceit and Wit are the features of the Metaphysical Poetry. The term Metaphysical poets was coined by the critic Samuel Johnson to describe a loose group of 17th century English poets whose work was characterized by the inventive use of conceits. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘The Captive Ladie’’ is a narrative poem by:

english.explanation: The Captive Ladie is a narrative poem by Michael Madhusudan Dutt. It was the first work of his literary career, published in book form in April, 1849. Dutt was a Bengali poet and dramtist, introduced Sonnets and blank verse to Bengali literature. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Arun Joshi's novel ‘‘The Apprentice’’ is in the form of:

english.explanation: Arun Joshi's novel The Apprentice is in the form of long monologue. Joshi (1939-93) was an Indian writer known for his novel The Strange Case of Billy Biswas. He won the Sahitya Akademi Award for his novel The Last Labyrinth in 1982. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘The Road’’ is a novel by:

english.explanation: The Road, (1961) is a English-language novel by Mulk Raj Anand. He won Padma Bhushan Award in 1967 and Sahitya Akademi Award in 1971 for Morning Face. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Manolin’’ is a name of______in Herningway's ‘‘The Old Man and the Sea’’.

english.explanation: Manolin is a name of character in Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea. Manolin is a young boy who is very hard working and wants to learn from Santiago. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Who among the following is known for Practical Criticism?

english.explanation: I.A. Richards is known for Practical Criticism, first published book in 1929. Practical Criticism was born of an experiment Richards undertook to discern the psychological foundations of reading and interpretation foundations of reading and interpretation and a means for readers to discover how they think and feel about poetry. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Uncle Tom's Cabin is written by:

english.explanation: Uncle Tom's Cabin; or, Life Among the Lowly is an anti-slavery novel by American author Harriet Beechor Stowe, published in two volumes in 1852, the novel had profound effect on attitudes toward African-Americans and slavery in the U.S. and is said to have ‘‘helped lay the ground work for the American Civil War’’. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following is not a work by William Blake?

options.prompt: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
Visions of the Daughters of Albion

english.explanation: Castle of Indolence is not a work by William Blake. It is written by James Thomson, a Scottish poet of 18th century in 1784. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘The Deserted Village’’ is a collection of poems by:

english.explanation: The Deserted Village is a collection of poems by Oliver Goldsmith published in 1770. It is a work of social commentary and condemns rural depopulation and the pursuit of excessive wealth. The poem is written DSSSB PGT English 28.06.2015, Tier-II 91 YCT in heroic couplets, and describes the decline of a village and the emigration of many of its residents to America. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.prompt: William Congreve: The School for Scandal

english.explanation: The School for Scandal is a comedy of manners written by Richard Sheridan. It was first performed in London at Drury Lane Theatre on 8th May, 1777. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: ‘On the Sublime’ is the work of:

english.explanation: On the Sublime is a Roman-era-Greek work of literary criticism dated to the 1st century C.E. Its author is unknown but is conventionally referred to as Cassius Longinus. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Who among these is not among to University Wits?

english.explanation: Ben Jonson is not the member of the University Wits. The university wits is a phrase used to name group of late 16th century English playwrights who were educated at the universities (Oxford or Cambridge). Prominent members of this group were Christopher Marlowe, Robert Greene and Thomas Nashe from Cambridge and John Lyly, Thomas Lodge and George Peele from Oxford. Thomas Kyd is also included but he was not from any of the aforementioned universities. Henced, option (d) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Imagism’’ is a school of poetry that flourished under the leadership of:

english.explanation: Imagism is a school of poetry that flourished under the leadership of Ezra Pound. Imagism was a movement in American and English poetry in the early 1900s emphasizing clear communication, concrete imagery, and plain diction. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: In_______external realism was abandoned in favour of a subjective approach.

english.explanation: In Expressionism external realism was abandoned in favour of a subjective approach. It was the dominant literary movement in Germany during and immediately after World War I. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: The use of expression ‘‘passed away’’ for ‘‘died’’ is an example:

english.explanation: The use of expression passed away for died is an example of Euphemism. The term euphemism refers to choose words or a phrase that can be used to convey something unpleasant sad or considered taboo. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: An unrhymed iambic pentameter verse is called:

english.explanation: An unrhymed iambic pentameter verse is called ‘blank verse’. Blank verse is any verse comprised of unrhymed lines all in the same meter, usually iambic pentameter. It was developed in Italy and became widely used during the Renaissance. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Which character in Hardy's ‘‘The Mayor of Casterbridge’’ sells his wife?

english.explanation: The Mayor of Casterbridge : The Life and Death of a man Character is an 1886 novel by the English author Thomas Hardy. The protagonist of the novel, Michael Henchard sells his wife for five guineas along with his baby daughter Elizabeth-Jane. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: A play designed for reading than for performance is:

english.explanation: A closet drama is a play created primarily for reading rather than production. Such type of plays are meant for peaceful reading in the lonely rooms that's why they are called as closet drama. These plays are often philosophic and thoughtful and sometimes they are poetic. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Who of the following is a science fiction writer?

english.explanation: Arthur Charles Clarke was an English science fiction writer an avid populariser of space travel, and a futurist of a distinguished ability. In 1961, he received the Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Tagore's Gitanjali comprises of_______poems.

english.explanation: The English version of Gitanjali is a collection of 103 English prose poems, which are Tagore's own English translations of his Bengali poems, and was first published in November, 1912 by the Indian society in London. In 1913 Tagore was awarded by the Nobel Prize in literature for English version of Gitanjali. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: J.M. Coetzee is a writer from:

english.explanation: John Maxwell Coetzee is a South African and Australian novelist, essayist, linguist, translator and recipient of the 2003 Nobel Prize in Literature. He is one of the most critically acclaimed and decorated authors in the English language. He won the Booker Prize (twice). Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Who among the following regarded Satan as the real hero of Paradise Lost?

english.explanation: Milton's Satan is one of the most powerful characters in his great epic, Paradise Lost. A wondrous feat of the imagination, Satan has received an abundance of attention from critics of Milton. One of his critics, John Dryden considered Satan as the real hero of Paradise Lost. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: In Canterbury Tales______appearance to be always busy and makes a should of his knowledge.

english.explanation: In Canterbury Tales, the Sergeant at Law, sometimes referred to as the Man of Law or the Lawyer appears to be always busy and makes a show of his knowledge . Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Who among the following is not diasporic writer?

english.explanation: Mahashweta Devi was not a diasporic writer. She was an Indian writer in Bengali and an activist. She was honoured with various literary awards such as the Sahitya Akademi Award (in Bengali), Jnanpith Award and Ramon Magsaysay Award along with India's civilian awards Padma Shri and Padma Vibhushan. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: The novel ‘Midnights’ Children was published in:

english.explanation: Midnight's Children is a novel published in 1981 by Indian-British writer Salman Rushdie, published by Joanthan Cape. The book won the Booker Prize and James Tait Black Memorial Prize in 1981. The technique of Magical realism finds liberal expression throughout the novel and is crucial to constructing the parallel to the country's history. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: The writer of ‘‘Trotter Nama’’ is:

english.explanation: The Trotter-Nama (1988) is a chronicle work by Irwin Allan Sealy. The novel traces the history of the Anglo-Indian community of seven generations of the Trotter family. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: The protagonist of Upamanyu Chatterjee's ‘English, August’ is:

english.explanation: The protagonist of Upamanya Chatterjee's English, August is Agastya. English, August was first published in India in 1988. The story of a young civil servant posted to a fictional rural town. A novel that captured the Zeitgeist of the 1980's. When India was uncertainly emerging from decades of economic isolation and ill-conceived socialism. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following is not a novel by Amitav Gosh?

english.explanation: Beethoven Among the Cows is a social realism novel written by Rukun Advani. The Circle of Reason, The Shadow Lines and The Culcutta Chromosome are novels written by Amitav Ghosh. Amitav Ghosh is an Indian writer, won the 54th Jnanpith award in 2018. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following is not a Satire?

english.explanation: The Alchemist is a novel by Brazilian author Paulo Coelho, published in English in 1993. It is not a satire but an adventure fiction. Don Quixote, The Medal and Don Juan are the best works on Satire. Hence, option (c) is correct. DSSSB PGT English 28.06.2015, Tier-II 93 YCT

en.value: The line ‘‘Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world’’ is by:

english.explanation: In The Defence of Poetry (1821), Shelley claimed that ‘‘poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world’’. This has been taken to suggest that simply by virtue of composing verse, they exert some exemplary moral power, in a vague unthreading way. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Hemingways novel ‘‘For whom the Bell Tolls’’ is set against the:

english.explanation: Hemingway's novel For whom the Bell Tolls is set against the Spanish Civil War. It was published in 1940 just after the end of the Spanish Civil War (1936- 39). The novel is regarded as one of Hemingway's best works, along with The Sun Also Rises, A Farewell to Arms and The Old Man and the Sea. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Man can be destroyed but not defeated’’ is a line from:

english.explanation: ‘‘Man can be destroyed but not defeated’’ is a line from The Old Man and the Sea (1952), a novella written by the American author Ernest Hemingway. It was the novel for whom Ernest was awarded by the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954. Hence, option (c) is correct answer.

en.value: ‘‘And faith unfaithful kept him falsely true’’ by Tennyson as an example for:

english.explanation: ‘‘And faith unfaithful kept him falsely true’’ by Tennyson as an example Oxymoron. An oxymoron is a figure of speech that juxtaposes concepts with opposite meanings within a word or in a phrase that is a self- contradiction. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘A thing of beauty is a joy forever’’ is a line from:

english.explanation: ‘‘A thing of beauty is a joy forever’’ is an opening line of Endymion (1818), a poem by John Keats. Keats dedicated this poem to the late poet Thomas Chatterton. The poem is written in rhyming couplets in iambic pentameter. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following novels is a Satire on the Gothic novel?

english.explanation: Northanger Abbey is a coming of age novel and a satire of Gothic novels written by the English author Jane Austen. It was published posthumously in 1817 with Persuasion. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Who's Afraid of Virginia Wool’’ is a______by Edward Albee?

english.explanation: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? is a play by Edward Albee first staged in October, 1962. It examines the complexities of the marriage of a middle-aged couple. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: The word ‘‘Catharsis’’ is taken from the field of:

english.explanation: Catharsis traces to the Greek word Kathairein, meaning to purge. Catharsis entered English as a medical term having to do with purging the body and especially the bowls of unwanted material. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Samuel Butler's ‘‘Hudibras’’ is a Satire on the:

english.explanation: Samuel Butler's Hudibras is a satire on the Cromwellians. Hudibras is a vigorous satirical poem, written in a mock-heroic style and published in three parts in 1663, 1664 and 1678. The action is set in the last years of the Interregnum before the restoration of Charles II as King in 1660. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following is not a work by Michael Ondaatje?

english.explanation: The Catcher in the Rye is not a work by Michael Ondaatje. It is a novel written by J.D. Salinger. The works written by Michael Ondaatje are The English Patient, Coming through Slaughter and Running in the Family. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Poetry is inspired Mathematical the line from:’’

english.explanation: Ezra Pound stated, ‘‘Poetry is a sort of inspired mathematics, which gives in equations, not for abstract figures, triangles, squares and the like, but for the human emotions.’’ Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: The soul of tragedy, according Aristotle is:

english.explanation: According to Aristotle, ‘‘Plot is the soul of tragedy’’. Aristotle goes on to describe the elements of plot, which include completeness, magnitude, unity, determinate structure and universality. Hence, option (d) is correct. DSSSB PGT English 28.06.2015, Tier-II 94 YCT

en.value: Bertolt Brecht is known for concept of:

english.explanation: Bertolt Brecht was a German dramatist, poet, theatre director and practitioner, who was the founder of a new theatre style called ‘‘Epic Theatre.’’ His epic theatre was in fact a revolt against the main stream modern theatre in which Brecht openly declares that theatre should be ‘political’. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: Diction means:

english.explanation: Diction refers to the linguistic choices a writer makes to effectively convey an idea, a point of view, or tell a story using syntax and word order. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Robert Browning is best known for his:

english.explanation: Robert Browning was an English poet and playwright whose dramatic monologues put him high among the Victorian poets. Dramatic monologue is a type of poetry written in the form of a speech of an individual character. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: ______applied the principle of Structurlism to anthropology.

english.explanation: Claude Levi-Strauss applied the principle of structuralism to anthropology. He was a French anthropologist and ethnologist whose work was key in the development of the theories of structuralism and structural anthropology. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: In ‘‘Death in Venice’’ the boy who attracts the Protagonist is:

english.explanation: Tadzio is a 14 years old Polish boy attracts the protagonist in Death in Venice. Death in Venice is a novella by German author Thomas Mann, published in

en.value: ‘‘Structure, Sign and Play’’ is a famous essay:

english.explanation: Structure, Sign and Play in the Discourse of the Human Sciences was a lecture presented at John Hopkins University on 21st October, 1966 by philosopher Jacques Derrida. The lecture was then published in 1967 as chapter ten of writing and difference. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: As per______the Metaphysical poets felt, ‘‘their thought as immediatly as th odour of a rose’’.

english.explanation: According to T.S. Eliot about Metaphysical poets, ‘‘their thought as immediately as the odour of a rose’’. This statement has been given in his essay. The Metaphysical Poets discusses a metaphysical characteristic, ‘‘Unification of sensibility’’. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Who disapproved Milton's ‘‘Lycidas’’ for its ‘‘Inherent improbability’’?

english.explanation: Samuel Johnson disapproved Milton's Lycidas for its inherent improbability. Johnson has recognised the poem as traditional pastoral because it depicted the idealized life of rural leisure. He also claims that Milton's poem is easy, vulgar and therefore, disgusting, whatever images it can supply are long ago exhausted and its ‘inherent improbability always forces dissatisfaction in mind.’ Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Who called Enlightement ‘‘the liberation of Mankind from his self-caused state of minority’’?

english.explanation: What is Enlightenment?, 1784 is a essay by the philosopher Immanuel Kant. He defines that ‘‘Enlightenment is the liberation of mankind from his self- caused state of minority’’. Further he exclaims the motto of the Enlightenment is ‘‘Sapere aude’’! – Dare to be wise! Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: James Joyce's ‘‘Ulysses’’ recounts the evnts of an ordinary day in:

english.explanation: Ulysses novel by Irish writer James Joyce, first published in book form in 1922. Joyce's Ulysses recounts the events of an ordinary day in Dublin. To give shape to this novel, Joyce takes Homer's Odyssey and makes it new. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: George Lukacs used the term_____for novel depicting social reality in a capitalist age on a broad scale.

english.explanation: George Lukacs used the term Bourgeois epic for novel depicting social reality in a capitalist age on a broad scale. Stony revolves around middle class and upper class society. Hence, option (b) is correct. DSSSB PGT English 28.06.2015, Tier-II 95 YCT

en.value: ‘‘The Two April Mornings’’ is a poem by:

english.explanation: The Two April Mornings is a poem by William Wordsworth. The poem was published in the series Matthew Poems (1815).

en.value: ‘‘Epithalamion’’ is a poem written celebrate a:

english.explanation: Epithalamion is a poem written to celebrate a marriage. It was written by Edmund Spenser to his bride. Elizabeth Boyle, on their wedding day in 1594 and first published in 1595 in London. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Lay Like the folds of a bright girdle furled’’ in Dover Beach is an example for:

english.explanation: Lay Like the folds of a bright girdle furled from Dover Beach is an example of cacophony figure of speech. Cacophony is a literary term that describes a blend of unharmonious sounds. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: The author of ‘‘A Vindication of the Rights of Woman’’ is:

english.explanation: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman : with strictures on political and moral Subjects (1792) written by British philosopher and women's right advocate Mary Wollstonecraft, is one of the earliest works of feminist philosophy. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: Mary Eliman's book ‘Thinking abc Women's discusses:’

options.prompt: Male bias in Freuds psycho analytic theory

english.explanation: Mary Eliman's book Thinking about Women's is a book of attitudes culled from the prose that literate men and women read and is, therefore, fashionable rather than profound. It discusses stereotypes of women in literature. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: ‘‘Sky lowered, and muttering thunder, some said drops

english.explanation: The above given lines are taken from the epic poem, Paradise Lost. In this book, John Milton declares that his aim in the book is ‘‘to justify the ways of God to men’’. The first version published in 1667, consists of ten books with over ten thousand lines of verse. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: ‘Negative Capability’ is associated with:

english.explanation: Negative Capability was a phrase first used by Romantic poet John Keats in 1817 to characterise the capacity of the greatest writers (Particularly Shakespeare) to pursue a vision of artistic beauty even when it leads them into intellectual conclusion and uncertainty opposed to a preference for philosophical certainty over artistic beauty. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: The critic who considered that Great literary works possess moral and cultural values is:

english.explanation: F.R. Leavis considered that great literary works possess moral and cultural values. Leavis believed that the role of literature in life is to confer a sense of significance to our routine existence and to question our habitual judgement, and great literature does both. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: ______locates the meaning of a text in its historical and cultural context.

english.explanation: New Criticism locates the meaning of a text in its historical and cultural context. It is a movement in literary criticism that born in 1980s. Its main claim is that the themes and meaning of literature are not universal and cannot be driven from the text alone. Hence, option (d) correct.

en.value: The term ‘‘Cultural Materialism’’ is associated with:

english.explanation: The term Cultural Materialism is associated with Raymond Williams. It emerged as a theoretical movement in the early 1980s along with ‘new historicism’ an American approach to early modern literature with which it shares common ground. It is used to describe a theoretical blending of leftist culturalism and Marxist analysis. Hence, option (b) is correct.

en.value: The novel form which deals with the development of the protogonist's mind and character is:

english.explanation: The novel form which deals with the development of the protogonist's mind and character is Bildungsroman for example Great Expectations, Jane Eyre etc. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: The term of lost generation is used to refer to:

options.prompt: American writers in the civil war period.
American writers of the decade following the
American writers of the decade following the
American writers of the Cold War period

english.explanation: The term of lost generation is used to refer to American writers of the decade following the World War I. The term was coined by Gertrude Stein and popularised by Ernest Hemingway in the epigraph of his novel The Sun also Rises. Hence, option (b) is correct. DSSSB PGT English 28.06.2015, Tier-II 96 YCT

en.value: ‘‘Can the subaltern speak’’? is the title of an essay by:

english.explanation: Can the Subaltern Speak? is the title of an essay by Gayatri Chakrovorty Spivak. It is all about the condition of women in the postcolonial era. The essay addresses the way in which subaltern woman is constructed, as absent or silent, someone who is not listened to. No one cares about them, what they think and what they say. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Who among the following is not a Pre-Raphaelite?

english.explanation: Among the given options Sylvia Plath is not a Pre-Raphaelite but she comes under the category of confessional poets. Later she committed suicide due to bipolar mental disorder. She was the wife of Ted Huges. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: The Norwegian playwright was popularised ‘‘problem plays’’ is:

english.explanation: The Norwegian playwright was popularised problem plays. Ibsen is often referred as the father of realism. He is well-known for his work A Doll's House. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: Which of the following plays is authored by Sophocles?

english.explanation: Among the given plays, Medea is not written by Sophocles, it was authored by Euripides, while rest of the plays in the options are by Sophocles. Hence, option (d) is correct.

en.value: In Greek Mythlology, Aphrodite goddess of:

english.explanation: In Greek Mythlology, Aphrodite is a goddess of sexual love and beauty, identified with venus by the Romans. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Sir Thomas More, then author of ‘Utopia’ belonged to:

english.explanation: Sir Thomas More, the author of Utopia belonged to England. Utopia was written in Latin and published in 1516. The book is a frame narrative primarily depicting a fictional island society and its religious, social and political customs. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: The author of the book ‘The Prince’ is:

english.explanation: The author of the book The Prince is Machiavelli. The main idea of the book is for a ruler, the ends justify the means. Machiavelli argued that rulers should strive to maintain or expand their position, even if immoral acts are necessary to accomplish that goal. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: Cervantes, the author of Don Quixote belonged to:

english.explanation: Miguel de Cervantes is the celebrated figure in Spanish literature. His novel Don Quixote revolutionized modern literature the central theme of the novel is that one must live life in a genuine way, passionately in spite of what other people think. Hence, option (c) is correct.

en.value: ‘The Playboy of the Western World’ is written by:

english.explanation: The Playboy of the Western World is written by J.M. Synge. It is a study on the nature of heroism and here worship. It refers to the main protagonist Christy Mahon, and how the plays with the fabric of truth. Hence, option (a) is correct.

en.value: The Divine Comedy narrates Dante's journey from:

options.prompt: Life on earth to life in the other world

english.explanation: The Divine Comedy by Dante Alighieri narrates Dante's journey from hell to paradise. The purpose behind this creation was to show people the horrors their souls would go through if they did not obey God's laws and did not live righteously. Hence, option (a) is correct.
